Hypothesis 2: on flat, specialist share 0.5, pi_K=0.1, the pi_C=0.5 cell had cum_R 110.0627 ± 7.9821, cum_D 9.2661 ± 3.0444, high-lambda cum_R 53.3168 ± 3.8689, high-lambda cum_D 4.4146 ± 1.3462, mean_coord_loss 0.6090 ± 3.2049e-04, mean_e 0.9714 ± 1.7608e-03, mean_iota 0.0662 ± 0.0131. The lowest cum_R on that flat slice was pi_C=0.5 at 110.0627 ± 7.9821; the lowest cum_D was pi_C=0.5 at 9.2661 ± 3.0444. Relative to flat pi_C=0 on the same slice (cum_R 138.3262 ± 7.9943, cum_D 12.6605 ± 4.4374, coord_loss 0.6311 ± 1.1292e-16, mean_e 0.9370 ± 2.5651e-03), pi_C=0.5 had lower cum_R and had lower cum_D; coord_loss was not higher and mean_e was not lower (lower mean_e would be more loafing). High-lambda periods are the high-lambda cumulatives above, not a separate reorganization. Hypothesis 3: at pi_C=0.5, specialist share 0.5, pi_K=0.1, modules cum_R was 108.9716 ± 10.2031 versus flat 110.0627 ± 7.9821, and modules cum_D was 9.2997 ± 3.4178 versus flat 9.2661 ± 3.0444; modules mean_coord_loss was 0.6051 ± 0.0334 versus flat 0.6090 ± 3.2049e-04. Across all 6 specialist-share by pi_K pairs at pi_C=0.5, modules had higher mean cum_R than flat in 3/6 pairs and higher mean cum_D in 4/6.
